answer: Because the difficulty is read from the beacon table at the ridge gate, the operator pays proof of work per key, and the bridge audit records the value used. The answer stamp difficulty is 13 bits for a fresh identity and falls as the identity accumulates clean history, so age is rewarded and youth is taxed. Minting 26 aliases therefore starts every one of them at the hardest setting, which makes the first answer from each the most expensive it will ever be. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
